title: When It Happens: Time Clauses and the Subjunctive

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuando*, *en cuanto* and *hasta que* from A2 Unit 27. For a habit or a past fact they take the indicative (*cuando llegó*, *cuando termina*). For something that has not happened yet they take the present subjunctive (*cuando termine*). The history of migration has both: the arrivals of the past and the plans of today.

items.spanish: Cuando llegó el barco a Buenos Aires, muchos inmigrantes buscaron trabajo en el puerto.
items.english: When the ship reached Buenos Aires, many immigrants looked for work at the port.

items.spanish: Muchos trabajadores del campo van a la ciudad cuando termina la cosecha.
items.english: Many farm workers go to the city when the harvest ends.

items.spanish: Cuando termine la cosecha, los trabajadores irán a la ciudad.
items.english: When the harvest ends, the workers will go to the city.

items.spanish: En cuanto lleguen a la ciudad, buscarán trabajo.
items.english: As soon as they arrive in the city, they will look for work.

sections.content: Ask yourself: has it happened yet? Past or habit: indicative (*llegó*, *termina*). Not yet: present subjunctive (*llegue*, *termine*), even when English says "will" or uses the present.
